nodes.title: the Hurnglim signature
nodes.statement: The Hurnglim system concerns objects called grixmis. There are exactly 3 of them: tezreld, vexyuk, muxlum. One operation is written #. One relation is written |>, read as "refines".

nodes.title: the Hurnglim combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x # y for every pair of grixmis is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the |> relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x and y, x # y is again a grixmi.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x, y, z: (x # y) # z = x # (y # z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x and y: x # y = y # x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a grixmi vexyuk with vexyuk # x = x # vexyuk = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a grixmi tezreld with tezreld # x = x # tezreld = tezreld for every x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every grixmi x: x |> x.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x, y, z: if x |> y and y |> z then x |> z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x and y, at least one of x |> y and y |> x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all grixmis x, y, z: if x |> y then (z # x) |> (z # y) and (x # z) |> (y # z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some grixmi x admits no grixmi y for which x # y and y # x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = tezreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every grixmi x: x # x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxlum, value = vexyuk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all grixmis x, y, z: if x # y = x # z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = tezreld, y = tezreld, z = vexyuk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all grixmis x and y: if x |> y and y |> x then x = y.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vexyuk, y = muxlum, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: rastpon grixmis
nodes.statement: A grixmi x is called rastpon when x # x = x.

nodes.title: grixmis that shenfal
nodes.statement: Two grixmis x and y are said to shenfal when x # y = y # x.

nodes.title: vintmorn collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of grixmis is vintmorn when x # y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the umbhob of a grixmi
nodes.statement: The umbhob of a grixmi x is the collection of grixmis y for which x |> y holds.

nodes.title: the hobka
nodes.statement: The grixmi vexyuk is called the hobka of the system. It is the unique grixmi that leaves every grixmi unchanged under #.

nodes.title: the zelmorn
nodes.statement: The zelmorn of the system is the collection of grixmis that shenfal with every grixmi.

nodes.title: the korrsol
nodes.statement: The korrsol is the collection of all rastpon grixmis.

nodes.title: the shenyuk of a grixmi
nodes.statement: The shenyuk of a grixmi x, written [x], is the smallest vintmorn collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a lumsib
nodes.statement: A grixmi f is a lumsib when f |> y holds for every grixmi y, that is, when the umbhob of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: aztpyr grixmis
nodes.statement: A grixmi x is aztpyr when x # x equals the hobka.

nodes.title: the glimmorn of a grixmi
nodes.statement: The glimmorn of a grixmi x is the number of grixmis in its shenyuk [x].

nodes.title: the bratez
nodes.statement: The bratez of the system is the collection of grixmis whose glimmorn is largest.

nodes.title: vexjen pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct grixmis x and y form a vexjen pair when x |> y and y |> x both hold, that is, when each lies in the umbhob of the other.

nodes.title: the hobka is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one grixmi e with e # x = x # e = x for every grixmi x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every grixmi unchanged.
Then e # f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e # f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the hobka lies in the zelmorn
nodes.statement: The hobka shenfals with every grixmi.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the hobka and x any grixmi.
Then e # x = x and x # e = x.
So e # x = x # e, which is what it means to shenfal.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the zelmorn.

nodes.title: the zelmorn is vintmorn
nodes.statement: If x and y both shenfal with every grixmi, then so does x # y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the zelmorn and let z be any grixmi.
Then (x # y) # z = x # (y # z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each shenfals with everything.
So x # y shenfals with z, and the zelmorn is vintmorn.

nodes.title: the shenyuk of a grixmi is vintmorn
nodes.statement: For every grixmi x, the collection [x] is vintmorn.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under #.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the shenyuk is contained in every vintmorn collection
nodes.statement: If S is vintmorn and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a grixmi is rastpon exactly when its glimmorn is one
nodes.statement: x # x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x # x = x then {x} is already closed under #.
So [x] = {x} and the glimmorn is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x # x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the glimmorn divides the number of grixmis breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every grixmi x, the glimmorn of x divides 3.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxlum, reach = 2, size = 3, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the shenyuk of a zelmorn grixmi stays in the zelmorn
nodes.statement: If x lies in the zelmorn then every grixmi of [x] lies in the zelmorn.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zelmorn is vintmorn.
[x] is the smallest vintmorn collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the zelmorn is one.

nodes.title: the korrsol is vintmorn
nodes.statement: If x and y are both rastpon then so is x # y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be rastpon.
The claim asks whether (x # y) # (x # y) returns x # y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: umbhobs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the umbhob of x, then the umbhob of y is contained in the umbhob of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x |> y and let z satisfy y |> z.
Transitivity gives x |> z.
So every member of the umbhob of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: the system has a lumsib
nodes.statement: Some grixmi lumsibs the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x |> y then (x # z) |> (y # z) for every grixmi z.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the umbhob of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: every grixmi lies in the zelmorn
nodes.statement: Every pair of grixmis shenfals.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zelmorn is defined by shenfaling with everything.
The claim is that x # y = y # x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every grixmi is rastpon breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x # x = x for every grixmi x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = muxlum, value = vexyuk, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some grixmi reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a grixmi whose shenyuk is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 2, size = 3, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x |> y then y |> x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = vexyuk, y = tezreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the hobka swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e # x equals the hobka for every grixmi x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = vexyuk, x = tezreld, value = tezreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.
